column1: bsubtilis_dryad_f4qrfj71n
column4: Data for: Extensive cellular multi-tasking within Bacillus subtilis biofilms
column17: Highest-value EXACT-SPECIES spatial candidate — B. subtilis is one of the seven. VERIFIED via the Dryad API, and the verification matters: the dataset's storageSize is 215.77 GB CUMULATIVE ACROSS VERSIONS while the CURRENT version totals 49.72 GB over 9 files. Budgeting from storageSize would overestimate by 4.3x. The four confocal archives are 4.36-6.46 GB each (Confocal-1..4.7z), so inspecting the README and downloading ONE archive is 4-6 GB, not 50. Parts of the study use prepared sections rather than intact volumes, so whether any archive provides an intact calibrated 3D biovolume must be checked at file level before it is treated as a pitch dataset.

column1: shewanella_dryad_8sc52
column4: Data from: In situ analysis of a silver nanoparticle-precipitating Shewanella biofilm
column17: EXACT SPECIES and the model's metal-reducing component. VERIFIED 5.142 GB via the Dryad API, matching the screening figure. NOT a pitch dataset: these are in-situ confocal Raman chemical scans, laterally calibrated, mapping cytochromes, flavins, polysaccharides and phosphate — not a conventional volumetric fluorescence biovolume series, and the optics were chosen to hold many cells in one focal plane. Retain to test exact-species chemical heterogeneity and to judge whether a homogeneous hydrated-effective material stays adequate once metal loading is present. Do not use it to select a.

column1: shewanella_zenodo_pedot
column4: S. oneidensis MR-1 on functionalised PEDOT:PSS surfaces
column17: EXACT SPECIES, and cheap to check: roughly 64.4 MB with a ~32.8 MB confocal archive plus live/dead and biofilm-formation spreadsheets. Metadata does not establish that the archive holds physically calibrated 3D z-stacks, so this is a low-cost metadata inspection rather than a known biovolume source. Identifier not verified in this pass.

column1: biofilmq_tutorial
column17: Not a calibration source — an EXTERNAL BENCHMARK. BiofilmQ thresholds 3D biofilm biovolume and subdivides it into user-sized cubic pseudo-cells, reporting cube volume fraction and interface properties without literal-cell segmentation. That is independent methodological support for the parcel semantics and the field harness. The check is agreement on the same input at the same cube size. It must NEVER become a runtime dependency: the package is deliberately numpy-only.

column1: pputida_microfluidics
column4: Pseudomonas putida biofilm in microfluidic channels
column17: Backup geometry and segmentation surrogate: raw Nikon confocal images with experimental parameters, processing code and derived thickness. Behind the V. cholerae deposit on verified metadata; hold unless that pilot fails.

column1: dradiodurans_zenodo_em
column17: REJECTED ON SCALE, not on quality. Exact species and a large high-resolution dataset, but its subject is cell ultrastructure in graphene liquid cells, not bulk biofilm architecture. A parcel is a coarse biomass unit; ultrastructure is several orders of magnitude below the scale at which a pitch is chosen, so no coarse-graining of it answers the pitch question.

column1: aniger_dryad_supplemental
column17: REJECTED ON MODALITY. Exact species, but the record holds supplemental figure files on fungal physiology rather than calibrated 3D biofilm stacks. Recorded so the same search is not repeated.

column1: cneoformans_deposits
column4: C. neoformans public deposits (flow cytometry / transcriptomic / figure data)
column17: REJECTED ON MODALITY. Searches surfaced flow cytometry, transcriptomic and figure-supporting data rather than reusable biofilm volumes. Note also that C. neoformans strains are commonly BSL-2 where other components are BSL-1, so this species drives the containment decision for any target campaign — see the biosafety fields in baseline_condition.csv.

column1: shewanella_holographic_motility
column17: REJECTED ON REPRESENTATIONAL GROUNDS, and it is the most instructive rejection here. An excellent exact-species dataset — 48 fps holographic recordings, 3D single-cell trajectories across four trials — that answers the WRONG question: it tracks swimming cells near an electrode, and a CPM cell ID is a computational biomass parcel, not an observable bacterium. Independent confirmation that single_cell_msd was correctly rejected as a seconds/MCS observable.

column1: target_consortium_search
column17: NO CANDIDATE FOUND. No volumetric dataset covers the modelled seven-species community, and no set of public datasets covers all seven components under one condition. Exact-species hits are fragmentary rather than a common calibrated reference system. This is a search result, not proof of non-existence — but it is enough to conclude that the target campaign should be designed rather than waited for.

column1: target_paired_material_search
column4: Paired 3D volume + wet mass + dry mass + matched blanks, one system
column17: NO CANDIDATE FOUND. The decisive missing record is the COMBINATION: same biological system, replicate-level calibrated 3D volume, wet mass, dry mass, matched hydrated and dry substrate blanks, documented surface-water removal, documented drying endpoint, same growth conditions. Published work supplies excellent methods and priors — one study derives density from dry weight per area over a CLSM biovolume built from live cells, dead cells AND EPS, which is exactly the volume-basis rule now enforced — but it yields X_total, not rho_wet.
